correctness.rationale: For finite-support input, the t-triangle bound and independent complex phase averaging sandwich the matrix quasi-norm between d^{-1/t} and 1 times an exactly solved diagonal optimization. Hölder gives the exact exponents r_{p,t} and q_t. The common-witness construction and Orlicz ℓ1 theorem establish the ideal dichotomy. For p>t, ℓ_r tails give compact approximations; for p<=t, coordinate-null columns and the elementary ℓ_t dominated-convergence identity yield the exact essential norm. The signed nearest-neighbor example has c_j asymptotic to j^{-1/q_t}; the finite-rank unbounded-row example confirms the boundary. Definitions, endpoints and quantified exponents were reconstructed and checked. Finite tests are supplementary only.

originality.rationale: A direct comparison with Araújo, Proposition 2.5, confirms that the known exact diagonal result has equal source/target exponent and no row-overlap cancellation. The new statement quantifies arbitrary complex finite-row-support mixing across all source/target exponents below one, gives distinct boundedness, compactness and summability thresholds, and proves their invariance under complex signs using a phase-averaging argument. Tomaz establishes lineability and Maddox establishes non-summability of the identity, neither the sparse matrix classification. Semantic research-record and targeted primary literature searches did not yield a theorem implying the combined new statement. Priority remains qualified by the risk of older generalized matrix criteria.
residual_risks: Older general quasi-Banach matrix/operator-ideal theory may contain an equivalent sparse-matrix equivalence not indexed under present terminology.

value.rationale: Uniform bounded row degree is a natural structural model for sparse difference, recurrence and discrete local operators. Unlike the known diagonal equal-exponent case, this gives a complete phase diagram for every pair of nonlocally convex source/target exponents and arbitrary complex cancellations: boundedness changes at p=t, compactness becomes automatic for p>t, while ideal membership is determined only by the target exponent. The sharp positive overlap loss and a signed compact operator outside every finite summing class explain necessity and demonstrate genuine separation of the invariants. This is a motivated classification, not a single arbitrary parameter evaluation.
